root_cause_label: Ignored Available apt-get in Favor of CPAN Rabbit Hole
one_sentence_failure_summary: After seeing apt-get in the PATH listing at step 12, the agent ignored it and instead spent the next 60+ steps attempting to build a custom web server via shell scripts and then installing HTTP::Daemon via CPAN, exhausting its budget on dependency chains, so that when it finally tried nginx via apt at step 74, an orphaned background Perl server already held port 8080.
t_err_evidence: At step 12, the agent listed /bin and /usr/bin and explicitly saw 'apt', 'apt-get', 'apt-cache', etc. in the output. Instead of using apt-get to install a web server (nginx, lighttpd, etc.), at step 13 the agent chose to build a custom server using mkfifo and shell scripts — ignoring the available package manager and locking into an increasingly complex DIY path.
t_commit_evidence: At step 44, the agent issued 'cpan HTTP::Daemon', beginning the CPAN rabbit hole. This consumed steps 44-73 resolving transitive dependencies (Module::Build::Tiny, ExtUtils::Config, ExtUtils::Helpers, ExtUtils::InstallPaths, HTTP::Date, Time::Zone, HTTP::Message, Clone, B::COW, Encode::Locale, IO::HTML, URI, Test::Needs, FFI::CheckLib, Test2::* modules, PkgConfig, etc.). Once this path was chosen, the agent had no budget left for a correct apt-based approach, making the failure locked in.
t_surface_evidence: Step 30 shows the first explicit error from the Perl server: 'Not enough arguments for accept at /tmp/server.pl line 9' — the first observable error signal from the Perl web server approach.
trigger_explanation: At step 12 the agent ran 'ls /bin /usr/bin' and received a full listing that prominently included apt, apt-get, apt-cache, apt-mark — all standard Debian/Ubuntu package manager tools. The correct action was to run 'apt-get install -y nginx' (or lighttpd, apache2, etc.) immediately. Instead, the agent proceeded to step 13 and began a hand-built server via named pipes and shell scripts, then shifted to a Perl-based server, ignoring the clear package manager signal until it was too late (step 74, when port 8080 was already in use).
forewarning_evidence: Steps 5-11 showed a cascade of missing tools (python3 not found, python not found, busybox not found, ncat not found), each signaling the environment lacks the expected quick-start servers. This should have prompted using apt-get before step 13. Steps 57-58 show repeated cpan Capture::Tiny commands (retry) — additional forewarning that CPAN path was failing.
